request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?

reply.reply: At enactment, CBO projected that the ACA together with the reconciliation bill would reduce federal deficits by $138 billion over 2010–2019 (CRS R41126, PDF p. 4). A later February 2011 baseline projected a $210 billion reduction over FY2012–FY2021 (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). That later projection counted substantial coverage costs alongside offsets: $1,390 billion in gross coverage-expansion costs, offset by $348 billion, for $1,042 billion net; overall, new revenues and direct-spending savings were projected at $1,252 billion (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). These were projections, not realized outcomes, and cover different time windows. See the [brief](output/briefs/case-20261025-181245-24d6.html).
reply.reasoning: Official CRS reports summarize the enactment-era estimate and a later CBO/JCT baseline. The brief distinguishes their periods and notes that both are projections.
